P3F obtains the same images through an approved internal registry mirror rather than by relaxing egress policy or by substituting a different image.

ruling_2026_08_29.statement: Upstream tag movement does not authorize a re-pin. The digests recorded above remain authoritative and are to be sourced from the approved internal mirror once it is provisioned.
ruling_2026_08_29.explicit_non_finding: The ratified digests are NOT invalid, superseded or compromised. A mutable tag moving to a newer image says nothing about the image these digests name; it is the expected behaviour of a mutable tag and precisely why the pins are by digest.
ruling_2026_08_29.consequence: base-image-digest-verification will continue to fail against live tag resolution until the mirror serves the ratified digests. That failure is the ratified MUST_HALT_ON_DIGEST_MISMATCH control operating as designed, not a defect to be silenced.

ruling_2026_09_05.statement: Preserve the existing ratified Node and Python base-image digests. Do not refresh or replace them, weaken the digest-verification gate, mark it non-blocking, change either Dockerfile FROM, or fabricate mirror coordinates. The container gate remains environment-blocked until an approved private OCI mirror is provisioned outside the repository. Repository configuration is authorized only after the owner supplies the real mirror host, repository prefix and GitHub Actions secret name.

The digest comparison is the first wall; the blob pull is the second, and it is unchanged by any pin.

rulings.rule: The ratified digest in deployment/governance-studio/base-images.json is authoritative until explicitly superseded through a controlled refresh (controlled_base_image_refresh below).
Dockerfile FROM references and platform declarations must continue matching that ratified digest exactly; mismatches remain blocking.

Movement of an upstream mutable tag such as node:22-bookworm-slim or python:3.11-slim-bookworm does not invalidate an already-ratified immutable digest. Tag drift becomes an advisory observation, never a required-status failure.
No workflow may automatically repin, substitute or approve a new digest.

Container builds must eventually pull the ratified digest from an owner-approved reachable OCI mirror. Missing mirror coordinates remain an explicit resource blocker, not a digest-conformance failure.

ruling_2026_09_05_separation.what_this_corrects: base-image-digest-verification conflated two different facts: whether the tree conforms to the ratified immutable digests (a property of tracked files, decidable offline) and whether Docker Hub's mutable tags still point at those digests (a property of an upstream registry that is expected to change). The second was failing the required container job every time a tag moved, which said nothing about the ratified image and could never be fixed without a re-pin the rulings forbid.
